<reason>Side A won by making the live choice easier to decide: a common retirement clock is either an unfunded wall or a date that yields when grids fail. Side B had a coherent incentive story and answered pressure honestly, but “keep the plants on and call it a surviving breach” undercut the motion’s operative claim without restoring a reason to chain major economies to that clock.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s retirement-day fork (shortages vs theatre) and the later use of B’s A1—plants stay on, so the common timeline becomes an annotation on delay rather than a phase-out.</best_rebuttal>
